children: By Stefanno Sulaiman and Gayatri Suroyo
Indonesia's government will make repayments of bank loans that are funding a national village cooperative programme, the finance minister said, as the first instalment falls due on Friday.

Suahasil Nazara, who was appointed as finance minister last week, said late on Thursday that the repayments will be made once the government verifies the funds were used as intended, including for the construction of cooperative stores in thousands of villages.
"This has been budgeted, the fund is ready, we will definitely pay," Suahasil said, noting 37 trillion rupiah ($2.1 billion) had been allocated in the 2026 budget.
"There must be verification for what have been built and how many," he said. "There's a validation process."

The bank loans are part of a complicated financing scheme for the "Red and White" village cooperative programme, an initiative of President Prabowo Subianto to stimulate rural economies as part of his drive to lift national growth to 8%.
Prabowo has said he wants the cooperatives to sell government-subsidised products, such as fertilisers and cooking gas, buy local produce, and offer cheap loans to villagers.
FOUR STATE BANKS LEND $13.6 BILLION

Under the scheme, state company PT Agrinas Pangan Nusantara is building 80,000 stores in villages across the vast archipelago, funded by 240 trillion rupiah of low-interest loans with 6-year tenures from four state banks.
Bank Rakyat Indonesia
, Bank Negara Indonesia
, Bank Mandiri
and Bank Syariah Indonesia
are the lenders.
When construction is completed, the loans will then be repaid by the government, rather than Agrinas Pangan, and eventually ownership of the cooperatives will be transferred to local communities.
The Cooperative Ministry and state auditors are in charge of the verification process.
The government has said its financing scheme would ensure a better outcome than previous schemes where funds were allocated directly to villages to use at their discretion.
QUESTIONS ABOUT SCHEME

Bank Mandiri and BNI have each disbursed 55 trillion rupiah to Agrinas Pangan, making up 3% and 6% of their respective gross loans, according to CreditSights, a research firm under Fitch Group, said in a note on September 22.
It did not detail lending by the other banks.

CreditSights said while the risk of non-payment is low, administrative delays are possible and that could cause the loans to be considered underperforming and  "could trigger ... temporary provisions and some earnings drag."

CreditSights said the long-term sustainability of each individual cooperative remained to be seen, noting a number of concerns about the scheme including a top-down rollout with a one-size-fits-all operating model, limited feasibility testing, and reports of poor site selections for some cooperative buildings.
It said it was also hard to assess Agrinas Pangan, the builder, as it was a newly formed state company with a limited track record.

The government has a target of constructing 35,000 cooperatives this year, with the rest to be built in 2027. As of Thursday,  25,977 cooperative stores have been built, according to a government monitoring dashboard.
